sections.title: Why Do We Use Layers?
sections.body: Sending data across the world is too big a job for one step, so we split it into small jobs — layers. Think of mailing a parcel: you write the letter (content), put it in an envelope (wrapping), write the address (label), and the truck carries it (transport). Each layer does ONE job well.
points: Each layer has its own job.
Each layer serves the layer above and below it.
Different companies can build products that still work together.

sections.title: The OSI Model — 7 Floors of a Building
sections.body: OSI is a teaching model with 7 layers. Learn what each floor does and which device lives there:

sections.title: Encapsulation — Packing the Parcel
sections.body: When data travels DOWN the layers, each floor adds its own label (header). Going UP at the other side, labels are removed one by one:
sections.code:
Your words          = Data
+ TCP header        = Segment   (L4)
+ IP header         = Packet    (L3)
+ Ethernet header   = Frame     (L2)
-> electric/light   = Bits      (L1)

sections.title: TCP/IP — The Real-World Version
sections.body: Real networks do not use all 7 OSI layers; they use the simpler TCP/IP model. Same ideas, fewer boxes. For the exam you must map them:

sections.title: Memory Tricks
points: Top-down: "All People Seem To Need Data Processing" (Application -> Physical).
Bottom-up: "Please Do Not Throw Sausage Pizza Away".
Devices: Switch = 2 letters = L2. Router = R looks like 3 = L3.
sections.tip: 💡 Exam tip: memorize "data → segment → packet → frame → bits". Questions love asking the PDU name at each layer.
